# BOOK 1 of 2: A Monk of Cruta (E. Phillips Oppenheim, 1894)

## Header
Public domain, Gutenberg #31535. Publisher J.S. Ogilvie, NY. Copyright 1894 F. Tennyson Neely. Chapters I–XXXVI, with epigraph-titles (e.g., Ch I "The Black-Robed Phantom 'Death'"; Ch II "The New Art"; Ch III "The Dancing Girl"; Ch IV/XI/XXI/XXVIII/XXIX/XXX/XXXI "Adrea's Diary" entries).

## Ch I (Cruta, deathbed)
- Dying man **Martin de Vaux** in a monastery on the island of **Cruta**, attended by **Father Adrian** (tall, gaunt priest; "Father Adrian" name) and servant **Gomez** (Gomez's master 25 years; Gomez thinks of Piccadilly house).
- Storm; 3 a.m. clock. Light seen at sea; Gomez spots it; bed pushed to window. Dawn. Steamer makes for bay, ignores 3 rockets warning. Yacht (large pleasure yacht) anchors; boat lowered.
- Martin's despatch-box. Visitors: **Paul** (Mr. Paul, steering, the young man, Martin's son, handsome; pale, distraught) and **Victor** (Victor Ferdinand Hirsfeld / "Count Victor"—the thin, elderly, wrapped-up "stranger", with soft black eyes, mocking smile). Paul had sought Victor from Monaco, Algiers, Cairo, Athens, Syracuse, Belgrade; found him at Constantinople as a Turkish army officer ("Monsieur le Captaine"); Victor kept Paul waiting 2 days. Paul threatened to throw him in Dardanelles.
- Victor refuses Martin's offer of fortune for giving up his power over "those whom you love, my slaves"; curses Martin. Martin shoots Victor dead through heart, then dies from effort. A dark-skinned thin child (**Adrea**) sobs over Victor's body. Priest asks "Dead?"—"Both dead."

## Ch II (Lady Swindon's reception, London)
- **Paul de Vaux** and brother **Arthur** ("no one ever called him anything else"; shorter, good-looking, violet in coat). Lady Swindon's afternoon; Arthur promised "novelty". Dancer performs to waltz-like violin music; in amber draperies; dusky face; heavy-lidded eyes. Paul is struck. Bishop present; Lady May (Westover) noted. Artists discuss "new art".

## Ch III (cab, Adrea's rooms)
- Paul leaves, hansom; Adrea (dancer) also calls cab on same street; she invites him to her rooms (back street, first floor; curtains divide room; dinner table). Arthur and **Leslie Horton** see them in cab; Adrea: "so far as I am concerned, that is of no consequence." Paul: "And it was for this then, Adrea Kiros, that you ran away from the convent St. Lucile! My God!"

## Ch IV (Adrea's Diary #1)
- Adrea: "little brown girl" Paul called her; Paul her guardian; hates women/men; diary-friend a morocco-bound book bought for a guinea in Bond Street. She invited Paul to dine; he left abruptly.

## Ch V (Vaux Court, Northumbrian Abbey)
- Mrs. de Vaux (mother, white-haired, duke's daughter). Paul at Vaux Court. Reynolds (grey-headed manservant) describes a Roman Catholic priest ("tall, rather thin, no hair on face, foreign accent") who spent 2 hours praying in chapel, asked when Paul returns. Paul recalls the Cruta deathbed; sees a dark figure in ruins. Paul sank onto sill.

## Ch VI (ride with Lady May; priest on avenue)
- Lady May Westover (fair, grey eyes, thoughtful; brother Westover). Paul tells May Arthur is infatuated with "Adrea Kiros" dancer. Paul's jump; spurs; Lady May's hopes of marriage. Paul's hand on May's; priest appears in avenue, grips May's horse rein; Paul recognizes him. Priest: "I wait for the moon to rise behind the ruins."

## Ch VII (ruins, midnight)
- Father Adrian prays in ruins. Paul meets him: priest says he left Cruta monastery; "closed forever"; "I am Father Adrian, priest...". He says he came to see Vaux home, "Martin de Vaux... died in my arms at Cruta". Reveals Martin confided secret to him. "A week" deadline mentioned later.

## Ch VIII (Arthur's rooms; Adrea)
- Arthur owes money; Paul discounts his acceptance (blue paper), burns it. Arthur's passion for Adrea ("Adrea is as necessary to me as the air"). Paul to lunch; Adrea invites Paul to tea at 5, Arthur can't come.

## Ch IX (Adrea's rooms, Grey Street; "Ah! how fair my weakness")
- Adrea on divan; Celeste her maid; Adrea recalls Constantinople childhood. Paul tempted; Adrea embraces; Paul resists (memory of Northumbrian moor, a woman's grey eyes = Lady May). Adrea furious: "I will know my father's secret!"

## Ch X (Adrea's letter; library)
- Paul's letter from Adrea, dated "18 GREY STREET, LONDON, W., Thursday"; she begs forgiveness, "little brown girl".

## Ch XI (Adrea's Diary #2: Grey Street, the grim building)
- Storm; Adrea sees a tall woman in black at a grim building (Roman Catholic institution), asking "Has Father Adrian called...?" Adrea calls her by name—she is **Nona?** no: the woman is **Madame de Merteuill** (identity: the woman, Adrea's ex-convent companion from Cruta). Adrea takes her home in cab; she faints.

## Ch XII (Father Adrian at Grey Street)
- Father Adrian visits Adrea; angry; says Adrea "deceived us," Cruta escape aided by him and the woman. Adrea reveals the woman (de Merteuill) is with her. Adrian and the woman meet.

## Ch XIII (Hunt; Major Harcourt cottage)
- Paul rides home from De Vaux hunt in storm; mare loses way near sea; reaches Major Harcourt's cottage; **Gomez** answers door (caretaker). Lady of house: **Madame de Merteuill** (tenant), tall, dark eyes, grey hair; her "step-daughter" is in London.

## Ch XIV (Madame de Merteuill's household)
- Paul recognizes her name; she startles. Gomez warns Paul to leave. Madame lies about step-daughter. Adrea enters; Paul stunned.

## Ch XV (Adrea at cottage; passion)
- Adrea: "A relative of mine came from abroad" (Madame de Merteuill). Adrea says she has given up engagements, will go on stage. Paul and Adrea embrace, admit love.

## Ch XVI (Father Adrian enters)
- Father Adrian appears in cottage with Madame de Merteuill; Adrian says he came to see her, bearing message from an old man; rebukes Adrea ("false to your Church...") ; Adrea defies him ("Your religion is a cold, dry farce"). Adrea: "Beware of him!"

## Ch XVII (Adrian's ultimatum)
- Adrian and Paul walk to Abbey ruins; Adrian threatens: Adrea must not be Paul's wife/friend/ward; Paul must swear never to look at her again, or Adrian will ruin Paul and name Martin a murderer. Paul asks "a week"; meet again "A week to-night".

## Ch XVIII (Lady May; Captain Westover)
- Lady May and Paul ride; Lady May heard Captain Westover and Captain Mortimer gossiping; cuts Paul off ("Please don't follow me"). Captain Westover (Lady May's brother) reveals Paul's settlement of £1000/yr to Adrea via solicitors Bevan & Bevan. Paul at cottage gate with Adrea ("cara mia").

## Ch XIX (cottage drawing-room, Madame de Merteuill's confrontation)
- Madame confronts Adrea and Paul: Martin de Vaux murdered Adrea's father (Count Hirsfeld / Victor). Adrea orders her out; Madame leaves. Arthur bursts in pale and muddy.

## Ch XX (Arthur confronts)
- Arthur demands explanation; Paul silent; Adrea scorns Arthur ("unformed, hysterical boy"); Arthur rides away into dark. Adrea kisses Paul.

## Ch XXI (Adrea's Diary #3)
- Adrea hates Father Adrian; she saw him at drawing-room, "Spy!" she says. Paul leaves. Madame (mother of Adrian) leaves in carriage for Cruta, weeping; says Adrian's influence. Adrea decides to confront Adrian.

## Ch XXII (Adrea vs Adrian; hate)
- Adrea confronts Adrian at cottage; he declares love, claims he has power to ruin Paul; his mother is Madame de Merteuill. Adrian walks to Abbey (Adrea's diary: he left, turning toward Vaux Abbey).

## Ch XXIII (Abbey, the confession)
- Storm night at Abbey ruins. Adrian tells Paul the full story: Martin de Vaux, Count of Cruta's daughter Irene, Hirsfeld etc. (The narrative is reported as Martin's confession.) Paul demands more.

## Ch XXIV (Martin's confession part 1)
- Martin met the Count of Cruta (Irene's father) in Palermo, visited Cruta; fell in love with Irene; Count refused; they eloped by yacht; Martin betrayed her. Count's curse: "The day will come!" Irene left him? (Irene ultimately "drowned" in Paris).

## Ch XXV (Martin's confession part 2)
- Irene left Martin, Count Victor Hirsfeld (Irene's suitor) appears; Irene's letter: "Marry me, Martin" on deathbed, at Cruta. Martin sails to Cruta; they marry in deathbed ceremony; he is thrust out.

## Ch XXVI (Martin at Cruta)
- Irene's funeral; Martin believes her dead; Count of Cruta bars him; Count Hirsfeld tells Martin Irene lives. Martin marries another; Paul born (Martin's son; heir). Hirsfeld's threatened visit.

## Ch XXVII (Hirsfeld's revelation; Irene's letter)
- Hirsfeld: Irene is alive; the boy is her son by Martin (Adrian? no—child is Paul). Martin's terms with Irene: money only. Irene's letter: at 25, son told; Paul (the son) claims De Vaux name. Martin sails with Paul to Palermo; Martin goes to Cruta; wounded by stabbing; dies in island monastery. Adrian narrates Martin's death; Martin's note to Paul c/o English Consul Palermo.

## Ch XXVIII (Adrea's Diary #4: Vaux Abbey)
- Adrea walks to Vaux Abbey; meets Lady de Vaux (Paul's mother, stately, with ebony stick); Paul found asleep at desk, grief-stricken. Lady de Vaux: "You are Adrea Kiros, the dancing girl!" Adrea tells Paul she loves him.

## Ch XXIX (Adrea's Diary #5: Paul; Cruta plan)
- Paul tells Adrea he is Martin's son only; Adrian has power; he will go to Cruta; Adrea begs him not to, reveals she was taken by Count of Cruta (her grandfather? Count of Cruta was her grandfather). Adrea (with Gomez) plans to kill Adrian. Gomez (Martin's loyal servant) whispers plan.

## Ch XXX (Adrea's Diary #6: walk to St. Bernard monastery)
- Adrea walks to monastery of St. Bernard at night; Adrian's mother = Madame de Merteuill, the daughter of Count of Cruta.

## Ch XXXI (Adrea's Diary #7: murder)
- Adrea lures Adrian to her room (Hermitage); he is in love; she stabs him with a Genoese dagger held by Gomez-handed; body dragged into wood. Adrea's diary: "It was done... Paul, my love."

## Ch XXXII (Count of Cruta, the castle)
- Old Count of Cruta (grandfather; tall, grey beard) on castle cliff; islanders Francesco, Antonio, Ferdinand, Guiseppe discuss the English ship returning; Guiseppe says yacht of "English lord" is Paul's.

## Ch XXXIII (Paul's arrival at Cruta)
- Paul and Adrea sail to Cruta on Paul's yacht; Adrea's sweet happiness ("fair weather ahead"). Guiseppe warns Paul; islanders take money, pass to monastery priest Father Bernard.

## Ch XXXIV (dying Madame de Merteuill)
- Paul reaches castle; monks; dying woman = Madame de Merteuill, real name Irene, daughter of Count of Cruta. Her account: Adrian (her son) was born of a false marriage; Marie (maid) impersonated her at marriage; the Count's plot to claim De Vaux estates for the Church; Irene dies "Martin, my love".

## Ch XXXV (Count's death, castle fire)
- Count of Cruta demands Paul's death; monks attack; Guiseppe rescues Paul; Count blows up castle; Guiseppe and Paul escape by boat; Count dies in explosion.

## Ch XXXVI (Adrea's suicide; end)
- Adrea writes final diary: Gomez warns of police; Paul learns of Adrian's murder (Times report). Paul confronts Adrea; she confesses; Paul rejects her; Adrea takes poison; Paul arrives too late with plan to sail to New York; she dies smiling; Paul swoons. "THE END."
- Back matter: ads for "The Mystery of the Ravenspurs" (Fred M. White) and "The Peer and the Woman" (Oppenheim).

# BOOK 2 of 2: Out of the Blue (Bertrand W. Sinclair, Gutenberg #73542)

## Ch I: A Retaining Fee (Fort Worth, April)
- **Rock Holloway**, young Texan rider, sorrel horse **Sangre**. Visits **"Uncle Bill" Sayre** (Trinity Bank, Fort Worth; Black-dialect speech; age 60; cattle owner). Rock's sister **Cecilia/"Cissy"** marrying a Brett; mother; father Steve Holloway (U.S. marshal at Abilene), uncle Tom ("Long Tom," Texas Ranger captain), cousin Ben Holloway (Ragged H, Milk River).
- Seventy Seven trail herd; boss **Elmer Duffy**; brothers **Joe, Ed, Mark** (Mark = bully, "Big" Duffy).
- Sayre's commission: Dave Snell (Maltese Cross, Trinity west fork) died; estate to children **Alice Snell** (21) and son (16). Executors: Sayre and **Buck Walters** (range boss, flashy, poker, women). Snell's range moved to Marias River, Montana (Fort Benton). Sayre gives $500 gold advance, $60/mo retainer ("retaining fee"). Rock to watch Buck, report.

## Ch II: In the Odeon (Clark's Ford, Nebraska, July)
- Clark's Ford on Platte crossing, saloon/dance hall "the Odeon." Rock meets **Al Kerr** (small Texan cowman, Capital K, Judith Basin, Arrow Creek; Lewistown). Mark Duffy drunk, lifts Kerr onto bar; Rock intervenes, shoots Mark dead. Rock rides off; realizes Duffy brothers will seek revenge.

## Ch III: The Steering Wheel (Montana/Canada, Sept–June)
- Rock joins trail herd of **Steering Wheel** brand (wagon boss; Canada, Old Man River, Fort MacLeod). Wintering at Steering Wheel ranch; boss **Dave Wells** (Texan, drawl). Suspicious herd of unbranded "doggies" with fresh Steering Wheel brand. Rock leaves; heads to Fort Benton.

## Ch IV: A Dead Double (Marias River, June)
- Rock packs mules for US cavalry near Fort Assiniboine. At TL Ranch on Marias, finds dead **Doc Martin** (ranch rider, looks exactly like Rock), shot from ambush. Woman **Nona Parke** (21, dark hair, gray eyes, proud; TL brand, Tom-Lowe?/TL) and daughter **Betty** (3, yellow hair, rag doll; calls Rock "Doc"). Nona's father died (horse fall), mother died at Betty's birth. Half-breed girl **Mary Vieux** helps.

## Ch V: Wrapped in Canvas
- Rock buries Doc Martin at dawn beside parents' graves under a cottonwood. Nona explains ranch history.

## Ch VI: Very Adroit Rock
- Nona hires Rock as Doc's replacement ($50/month). Elmer Duffy arrives; Rock poses as Doc Martin to Duffy. Duffy denies shooting Doc. Rock rides with Nona; Nona's step/hidden calves; Rock plays as Doc.

## Ch VII: Mariners
- Rock on round-up near White Springs; meets **Alice Snell** (yellow hair, dark brows, blue-violet eyes, green corduroy riding skirt, carved saddle; calls him Doc) and TL rider **Charlie Shaw** (blue-eyed youth ~20). **Buck Walters** (big, tall, gray-agate eyes, well-dressed) stares at him. Nona and Rock grow close.

## Ch VIII: Getting Down to Cases
- Charlie tells Rock "whispers" he's rustling with **Burris boys** (behind the Goosebill). Rock reveals identity to Charlie. Doc had been warned by Buck; Doc had found "branding corrals" in the Sweet Grass hills. Nona sends Rock to Fort Benton for hay hands.

## Ch IX: Ordered South (Fort Benton)
- Fort Benton (Grand Union Hotel). Rock sees Buck Walters with Dave Wells at bar; poses as Doc, then reveals as Rock Holloway. Buck threatens Rock: "go South"; Rock refuses; Buck: "I'll have you put away... inside of forty-eight hours."

## Ch X: Thirty Angry Men
- Alice Snell warns Rock: Buck and Elmer plan to hang "Doc Martin" for rustling. Vigilante party (30 riders) arrives. Rock holds them at bunkhouse with carbine; Charlie joins; Nona defends. Rock proves identity (Sorrel "JB" horse, black "Bleeding Heart"). Buck calls Doc a rustler, Elmer backs down. Alice rejects Buck: "I hate you."

## Ch XI: Riders on a Rise
- Nona/Rock talk; Alice stays at TL. Charlie and Rock ride to bring horses; ambushed by **Joe Stack** and **Bill Hurley** (hired by Buck, $500). Hurley dies; Rock shoots Stack's horse; captures Stack (Maltese Cross horse).

## Ch XII: Stack Decides to Talk
- Rock tortures Stack (foot to fire); Stack confesses: Hurley shot Doc Martin; Buck paid $500 for Rock's death. Rock lets Stack go on Maltese Cross horse, south.

## Ch XIII: On the Warpath
- Nona bandages Rock's head wound (scalp slash). Buck has left with pets to North. Rock kisses Nona goodbye; rides to Judith Basin to Al Kerr (Capital K); gets 12 men; telegram from Sayre ("Act on your own judgment... Coming north").

## Ch XIV: Hot on the Trail
- Telegram from Billings; Sayre "Suspected this." Rock rides to Capital K; goes north with a dozen Capital K riders. Charlie joins; reveals Buck's crew at Sweet Grass hill (Gold, West, East Buttes).

## Ch XV: Popping Guns
- Rock and Charlie scout hidden corrals on East Butte; branding Steering Wheel brand (rebranding stolen Maltese Cross cattle). Lookout shoots Charlie (wounded). Rock flees; horse shot; ambush; Buck Walters charges with black horse; Rock kills Buck; black horse dies on him.

## Ch XVI: "Certainly Not Sad."
- Sayre arrives; Rock shows he "rebranded" Maltese Cross to Steering Wheel (Buck's scheme; Buck bought 1,200 head with $25,000 loan). Sayre asks Rock to run Maltese Cross; Rock hesitates. Rock returns to TL; Elmer Duffy present; they shake hands. Charlie wounded, sent to Benton. Rock reveals love to Nona; she says "I like you a heap," then "I'm certainly not sad!" [Transcriber's note: first appeared Blue Book Magazine July 7, 1927.]

# Notes on structure
- Book 1: 36 chapters; 5 Adrea diary entries (IV, XI, XXI, XXVIII–XXXI).
- Book 2: 16 chapters, ends with transcriber's note.
